scope: Sprint 10 Phase 10/15 — verify NSW and VIC compute canonical metrics using the same shared formula (warehouse/config/market_metrics.yml), spot-checked against real branch data
method: Live SQL recomputation of gross_yield_pct = round((median_weekly_rent_latest * 52 / median_sale_price_12m) * 100, 2) against real rows on the branch, compared to the stored value.

checks.result: PASS — exact match on all 6 sampled rows (e.g. Port Melbourne: stored 2.67, recomputed 2.67; Cranbourne: stored 4.22, recomputed 4.22)
checks.detail: VIC's yield is computed by load_vic_market_intelligence_to_branch.mjs directly from the same sales-pick and rent-latest values that also populate median_sale_price_12m and median_weekly_rent_latest — single dwelling-type pick, exact formula match expected and confirmed.

checks.result: EXPECTED DIVERGENCE, not a bug — recomputation from the wide-row median_sale_price_12m/median_weekly_rent_latest fields does not match the stored gross_yield_pct for several rows (e.g. Hornsby: stored 4.715 vs naive recompute 2.02)
checks.detail: This is by design, not a formula inconsistency: NSW's yield_latest CTE (rebuild_nsw_snapshots_after_reconciliation.mjs, inherited from Sprint 9) picks the best-available REAL dwelling-type row (never the 'all' bucket) for yield, which may use a different dwelling-type/period pairing than the wide-row snapshot's headline 'latest' sales/rent fields. This is exactly why yield_sale_period_used and yield_rent_period_used exist as separate columns — to record which period was actually used for yield, since gross_yield is defined (market_metrics.yml) as never forced into same-calendar-period alignment. Naive recomputation from the headline fields is the wrong test for NSW; the correct test is recomputing from the specific dwelling-type row at yield_sale_period_used/yield_rent_period_used, which was not re-verified this pass (out of scope — NSW's yield methodology was already verified in Sprint 9).

shared_scenario_check.detail: meta.metric_assumption (scenario standard_20pct_deposit_30yr_pi) has no jurisdiction/state column — verified via direct query (warehouse/reports/vic_supply_demographics_affordability_report.json). Both NSW's and VIC's snapshot-builder scripts read the same scenario_code and mart.national_interest_rate_context rows, so the deposit percentage, loan term, repayment type, and rate source are structurally identical, not independently re-implemented per state.

dwelling_type_vocabulary_check.detail: CANONICAL_DWELLING_TYPES in lib/warehouse/contracts.ts remains exactly 6 values, unchanged by this sprint. VIC's build_vic_sales_local_store.mjs and warehouse/config/vic_dwelling_type_mapping.yml only ever assign values from this shared vocabulary (detached_house, apartment_unit, residential_land) — never a jurisdiction-specific value outside it. Verified in warehouse/scripts/sales/validate_vic_sales_local_store.mjs's confidence/gate checks and lib/warehouse/contracts.test.ts's new VIC fixture tests (10/10 pass).

sample_size_confidence_check.detail: SAMPLE_SIZE_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLDS (high>=30, medium>=10, low>=5) in lib/warehouse/contracts.ts is shared/immutable across jurisdictions. VIC's build_vic_sales_local_store.mjs applies the identical numeric thresholds to VPSR's published transaction_count wherever available, falling back to a coarser flag-based tier only where the source itself publishes no exact count (documented explicitly in VIC_DWELLING_TYPE_CLASSIFICATION.md, not a redefinition of the thresholds themselves).

notes: This report validates that the FORMULA and VOCABULARY are shared, not that every stored value is independently re-derivable from only the wide-row snapshot's headline fields — NSW's yield methodology intentionally uses a more specific period pairing than the headline fields, which is the correct, documented behaviour, not a defect.
